title: Runtime Observability and Self-Heal Orchestration Manual
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document describes the observability-driven self-healing orchestration layer that sits above the serving runtime. It defines telemetry contracts, the priority-rebalancer and automatic fallback controllers, validation/benchmarking harnesses, and an operational runbook for investigation and rollback. The goal is to keep customer-facing SLOs intact while enabling safe automated remediation of common degradation patterns (kernel stalls, KV cache thrash, NUMA imbalance, and soft OOMs).

Why this exists
---------------

Redwood’s runtime is highly-optimized but operates in multi-tenant, bursty environments. Human intervention is slow for tail-latency regressions and kernel regressions that require quick mitigation. The self-heal orchestrator reduces MTTI/MTTR by safely applying corrective actions (routing, shedding, kernel rollback, re-quantization, and temporary QoS changes) under tight observability contracts.

Scope
-----

This manual covers:
- Telemetry signals and minimal observability contract
- Recovery actions and safety gates for each failure class
- Priority-rebalancer logic and knobs
- Profiling & benchmark validation recipe for automated remediations
- Incident runbook with checklists, CLI commands and escalation path
- Known limitations and migration notes

Architecture (text diagram)
-------------------------

Serving runtime node(s)  <-->  Telemetry collector (trace/metrics/logs)  <-->  Orchestrator (policy engine + decision log)  <-->  Remediation drivers (router, KV manager, kernel-toggle controller)

Components and responsibilities
--------------------------------

1) Telemetry collector (observability-adapter)
- Aggregates kernel-level traces (kernel_id, kernel_latency_p50/p95/p99), per-request token counts, KV cache hit-rate by prefix, allocator pressure, and GPU thermal/power events.
- Exposes an ingest API (protobuf over gRPC) with 10s aggregation windows by default.

2) Policy engine (self-heal-orch)
- Consumes summarized telemetry; evaluates policies (SLA preservation, unit-cost guardrails).
- Emits decisions as append-only decision logs (immutable), with a decision_id, rationale, and safety checks.

3) Remediation drivers
- Router: adjusts routing weights across model variants/regions.
- KV manager: toggles aggressive prefetching and evictions; issues warmup hints.
- Kernel controller: enables/disables kernel variants or rolls back kernel bundles per-node.

Telemetry contract (must be implemented by services sending signals)
------------------------------------------------------------------

Required metrics (names are canonical; agents must map to these names):
- runtime.request.latency.p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- kernel.exec.latency.p50, p95, p99 (ms) per kernel_id
- kvcache.hit_rate (0..1) per tenant and prefix-class
- allocator.free_bytes and allocator.fragmentation_pct per host
- gpu.utilization_pct, gpu.power_watts, gpu.temperature_c
- trace.sample: end-to-end trace with tags: kernel_id, tenant_id, model_variant, request_surface, slot_id

Ingestion SLA and retention
- Ingestion latency: <= 15s for 10s aggregates for production clusters.
- Minimum retention for decisioning: 1h of high-resolution traces and 14d of aggregated metrics.

Policy & decision safety gates
-----------------------------

Every automatic remediation must satisfy three gates before action:
1) Evidence gate: at least two independent signals (latency spike + kernel exec tail) above threshold for >= 3 evaluation windows.
2) Impact gate: simulation/estimate that remediation preserves SLO for at least 90% of active requests.
3) Rollback gate: a precomputed rollback path exists and has been smoke-validated in staging within the last 7 days.

Priority rebalancer algorithm (summary)
--------------------------------------

Purpose: dynamically rebalance kernel priority credits across concurrent workloads to prevent priority inversion and kernel starvation.

Inputs:
- queue_length_by_priority (short, mid, long)
- kernel_exec_latency_p95_by_priority
- token_rate_by_priority
- slot_utilization and free_memory_estimate

Core heuristic (pseudocode):
```
if kernel_exec_latency_p95_by_priority['short'] > SLO_short * 1.4 and slot_utilization < 0.8:
    transfer_credit(from='background', to='short', amount=min(credit_pool*0.2, deficit_estimate))
elif allocator.fragmentation_pct > 70%:
    throttle_background_jobs(pressure=0.3)
else:
    decay_transfers()
```

Knobs and configuration table
------------------------------

| param_name | default | range | description |
|-----------|---------:|------:|------------|
| evaluation_window_s | "10" | "5..60" | Aggregation window for decision inputs (seconds). |
| evidence_confirmation_windows | "3" | "1..10" | Number of windows required to confirm an event. |
| max_credit_transfer_pct | "0.2" | "0..0.5" | Maximum fraction of credit pool transferable in one decision. |
| emergency_fallback_timeout_s | "30" | "10..300" | Time to wait for a successful rollback before expanding mitigations. |

Profiling and benchmark validation recipe
----------------------------------------

Automated mitigation must be validated using a deterministic synthetic workload prior to roll-to-prod. Use the runtime-benchmark harness (see config snippet below).

YAML example (benchmark job for validation):
```
benchmark_job:
  name: "self_heal_validation_burst_short_priority"
  traffic_profile:
    - shape: "sudden_burst"
      duration_s: 120
      qps: 800
  request_surface: "short-chat"
  sample_tracing: 100%
```

Validation criteria:
- No P99 regression > 10% vs baseline for the primary route.
- Fallback actions reduce P99 by >= 20% in degraded scenarios within 45s.
- No data-loss or request duplication observed in trace reconciliation (trace IDs monotonic).

Runbook: Incident triage and automated remediation checklist
-----------------------------------------------------------

1) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   1.1 Check SLO dashboard: runtime.request.latency.p99 and kernel.exec.latency.p99.
   1.2 Correlate with recent decision log entries: `self-heal/decisions` feed.
   1.3 Snapshot a 2-minute trace sample for the impacted tenant(s).

2) Confirm pattern (10-20 minutes)
   2.1 Ensure evidence gate satisfied: at least two signals across 3 windows.
   2.2 If evidence gate not satisfied, escalate to oncall and increase sampling to 100% for 5 minutes.

3) Execute remediation (automation preferred)
   3.1 For kernel tail regressions: trigger kernel rollback for impacted nodes via kernel controller: `redwoodctl kernel rollback --nodes <node-list> --bundle <bundle-id>`
   3.2 For KV cache thrash: change eviction policy to `freq=aggressive` and issue prefetch hints: `redwoodctl kv adjust --prefix <prefix> --policy aggressive`
   3.3 For NUMA-induced latency: enforce numa-affinity hint on new allocations: `redwoodctl host set-affinity --host <host> --policy strict`

4) Observe and validate (20-45 minutes)
   4.1 Ensure remediation decision recorded and visible in decision-log with decision_id.
   4.2 Validate P95/P99 trends and check no cascading failures.
   4.3 If remediation fails to reduce P99 within emergency_fallback_timeout_s (default 30s), expand to next mitigation step (e.g., route to fallback variant).

5) Post-incident (within 24h)
   5.1 Open a post-incident review with decision-log export and kernel trace bundles attached.
   5.2 Add a regression test to the microbenchmark suite that reproduces the trigger pattern.

Quick CLI commands
-------------------
- View recent decisions: `redwoodctl decision tail --since 10m`
- Force a manual decision abort: `redwoodctl decision abort --decision-id <id>`
- Increase telemetry sampling: `redwoodctl telemetry sampling set --scope tenant:<t> --rate 100`
- Rollback kernel bundle: `redwoodctl kernel rollback --nodes <nodes> --bundle <bundle>`

Benchmarking suite integration points
------------------------------------

- The orchestrator integrates with the benchmark suite via a webhook that runs validation jobs when a remediation policy is created/updated.
- Validation must run on a staging fleet that mirrors production heterogeneity (GPU types, slot sizes, and NUMA topologies).
- Reports are stored in the benchmark-results bucket under `self-heal-validations/` with JSON results and trace artifacts.

Release notes (summary of notable changes)
------------------------------------------
- 2026-01-18: v0.9 release — initial production rollout of self-heal orchestrator with evidence & rollback gates.
- 2026-02-08: v1.0 release — added priority-rebalancer, KV manager driver, and admission gate improvements.
- 2026-03-02: v1.1 patch — tightened evidence confirmation windows default from 5 -> 3 windows and fixed decision-log truncation bug.

Known issues and mitigations
---------------------------
- Issue: rare false positives when short-lived network stalls cause spurious kernel p99 spikes.
  Mitigation: evidence gate requires multiple signals and decision engine now cross-checks host-level network err_count.
- Issue: rollback path sometimes fails when staging rollback has drifted from prod kernel metadata.
  Mitigation: staging bake jobs now run nightly and verify bundle checksums; policy engine rejects auto-remediation if last staging verification is older than 7 days.

Operational ownership and SLAs
-----------------------------
- Owner: Serving Runtime SRE (oncall roster: runtime-sre@redwood.internal)
- Escalation: runtime-sre -> Runtime Platform lead -> Eng oncall (pager) -> CTO (for customer-impacting incidents)
- Operational goal: automated mitigations should resolve 70% of transient P99 spikes within 60s in non-critical tenants.

Privacy and safety considerations
--------------------------------
- Decision logs are treated as internal telemetry; do not be exported to customer logs.
- Any remediation that may route customer traffic across regions requires prior legal review (see `security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions`).

Appendix A — Decision log schema (flattened example)
---------------------------------------------------
- decision_id: string
- created_at: ISO8601 timestamp
- trigger_signals: comma-separated list
- rationale: short string
- action: short string (e.g., kernel_rollback, adjust_kv)
- impacted_nodes: comma-separated list
- rollback_action: short string
- safeties_checked: comma-separated list

Appendix B — Smoke-validation checklist for kernel rollback
----------------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm kernel bundle checksum in staging: `redwoodctl kernel verify-staging --bundle <bundle>`
2) Run microburst validation (see YAML above) against the staging mirror.
3) Ensure no more than 1% increase in token-drop-rate and zero duplication in traces.
4) Mark bundle as staged: `redwoodctl kernel mark-staged --bundle <bundle>`

--------------------

- Incident orchestration matrix: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-incident-orchestration-and-capacity-decision-matrix-2026

If you are implementing or modifying policies, add unit tests for both the evidence gate logic and the rollback gate, and request an architecture review from the runtime-sre team before enabling in production.
